scenes.heading: Geometry and measurement problems
scenes.sub: A few facts, used one after another
scenes.say: Geometry questions give you a diagram and ask for a missing angle, length, area or volume. A handful of facts, used one after another, solves almost all of them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A detective fills in one clue at a time until the case is solved
scenes.science: Write each angle you find on the diagram until x is surrounded
scenes.breaks: a detective may guess; you must name a fact for every step.
scenes.say: Be a detective. Write every angle or length you can find straight onto the diagram, one clue at a time, until the unknown is surrounded. Unlike a detective, though, you never guess — every step uses a fact.

scenes.heading: Angle facts
scenes.say: Learn the angle facts. A straight line is one hundred and eighty degrees, around a point is three hundred and sixty, and a triangle is one hundred and eighty. A polygon's angles add to n minus two, times one hundred and eighty.
scenes.caption: A straight line is 180°, around a point is 360°, and a triangle is 180°. A polygon's angles add to (n − 2) × 180°.

scenes.heading: Angles on a straight line
scenes.say: First the straight line, then three angles: fifty-seven degrees, x, and forty-eight degrees. They sit on a straight line, so they add to one eighty. Fifty-seven plus forty-eight is one hundred and five, so x is seventy-five degrees.
scenes.caption: A straight line with three angles: 57°, x and 48°. They add to 180°. 57 + 48 = 105, so x = 75°.

scenes.heading: Split a composite shape
scenes.say: Here's an L shape: twelve centimetres along the bottom, eight up the right, five across the top, three up the left. The missing sides are seven and five. Cut along the dashed line: seven times three is twenty-one, five times eight is forty, so the area is sixty-one square centimetres.
scenes.caption: An L shape: 12 cm bottom, 8 cm right, 5 cm top, 3 cm left. Missing sides are 7 and 5. 7 × 3 = 21 and 5 × 8 = 40, so the area is 61 cm².

scenes.heading: Volume of water
scenes.question: Tank 50 cm by 40 cm, water 18 cm deep. How many litres?
scenes.say: A tank is fifty by forty centimetres, with water eighteen centimetres deep. Fifty times forty times eighteen is thirty-six thousand cubic centimetres. A thousand cubic centimetres is one litre, so that's thirty-six litres.
scenes.caption: A tank 50 cm by 40 cm, water 18 cm deep. 50 × 40 × 18 = 36 000 cm³. 1000 cm³ = 1 L, so 36 litres.

points: F and Z angles equal, C adds to 180°
Units the same before you start
scenes.say: Quick recap. Know your angle facts, split or subtract for composite shapes, multiply three lengths for volume, and make the units match first. Now try the practice questions!
